# Data and measurement

The unit of observation is an economy at a World Bank Enterprise Survey wave.
FIN14 measures the share of eligible firms with a bank loan or line of credit.
The underlying question covers a loan or credit line from a financial
institution. National rows require all six demographic and combined
breakdown dimensions to be total. Indicators join on economy and survey year.

```{r data-tables}
show <- function(x, caption = NULL, digits = 2) {
  knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE,
               booktabs = TRUE)
}
show(coverage, "Economy coverage under the alternative rules")
```

The latest FIN14-observed wave and the latest wave in the union of archived
WB_ES indicators differ for `r nrow(wave_disagreements)` economies. The
union uses rows in this snapshot, so the check covers its published vintage.

```{r survey-years}
show(pitch_years, "Survey vintage in the pitch and the rebuilt sample")
```

## Reconciliation with the visual abstract

```{r pitch-statistics}
show(cbind(Indicator = rownames(pitch_summary), pitch_summary),
     "Same-wave pitch variables, with the original units and dummy coding")
```

```{r rounding-differences}
show(pitch_differences, "Differences at displayed precision", digits = 5)
```

Both displayed differences are reproducible by rounding first to two decimal
places and then to one. The original rounding procedure is undocumented.
FIN11 includes a tiny floating-point overshoot at the upper endpoint.

## Indicator direction and sample selection

WBES documents BREADY\_DISP3 as weighted disagreement about court
independence and impartiality, following its September 2025 scale revision.
CRIME9 and BREADY\_DISP6 increase with perceived severity of a court obstacle.
The latter scores all response levels. See the
[WBES indicator guide](https://www.enterprisesurveys.org/content/dam/enterprisesurveys/documents/methodology/Indicator-Description.pdf).

```{r direction-and-selection}
show(direction_values, "Same-wave checks for court doubt")
```

The archived minimum and maximum occur in `r paste(subset(direction_values, BREADY_DISP3 == min(study$BREADY_DISP3))$economy, collapse = ", ")`
and `r paste(subset(direction_values, BREADY_DISP3 == max(study$BREADY_DISP3))$economy, collapse = ", ")`.
The pitch note cited Germany and Pakistan as the extremes.

```{r direction-correlations}
show(cbind(Indicator = rownames(direction_cor), as.data.frame(direction_cor)),
     "Correlations of the orientation checks")
```

```{r selection}
show(profiles, "Observed credit and vintage by inclusion status")
```

```{r regions}
show(region_counts, "Coverage by World Bank region")
```

EAS is East Asia and Pacific, ECS Europe and Central Asia, LCN Latin America
and the Caribbean, MEA Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan,
NAC North America, SAS South Asia, and SSF Sub-Saharan Africa.

The archived QoG variable is from La Porta et al. (1999). Code 1 is English
common law, codes 2, 4 and 5 are French, German and Scandinavian
commercial-code origins, and code 3 is Socialist. Missing codes remain
missing in the primary origin comparisons. The all-known contrast pools
codes 2 through 5. The named civil-code contrast uses codes 2, 4 and 5
as the comparison group. The generated origin audit distinguishes absent
economy rows from matched rows lacking a code and lists the pitch and sensitivity
classification. See the [QoG codebook](https://datafinder.qog.gu.se/variable/lp_legor).

```{r origin-counts}
show(origin_counts, "Archived legal-origin coverage")
```

GRAFT3 covers six public transaction types and treats refusals as affirmative
responses. DISP2 is conditional on reporting a dispute. FIN11 describes the
latest loan or line among borrowing firms. FIN20 records non-application
attributed to sufficient funds in the last fiscal year.

# Model and hypotheses

The design starts with a simple OLS regression on court doubt, then adds
bribery exposure, firm size and legal origin. The study estimates
associations across economies.

# Estimation and diagnostics

Estimation will follow the data audit. Planned outputs include conventional and
HC3 inference, model fit, joint tests, Durbin-Watson, Breusch-Pagan and VIF.
